source.title: Ascent Fails to Forget
source.authors: Ioannis Mavrothalassitis; Pol Puigdemont; N. Levi; V. Cevher

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests gradient-ascent and descent-ascent unlearning performance using a different benchmark and measure (KLoM), and reports when these methods fail or degrade other-set performance.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates unlearning quality, not recovery attacks. Figures 1–3 give some explicit qualitative findings; Figure 6 shows sweeps over configurations, without tabulated per-configuration values. Figure 7 reports retain-set KLoM and says its patterns are nearly identical to Figure 6. The MNIST/FashionMNIST table compares pretrained and oracle models, not results of an unlearning attack, so it is not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study is about sample-level data unlearning in image classifiers (ResNet-9 on CIFAR-10). Its measure is KLoM, the distance of predictions from a retrain oracle, plus theory on logistic regression. No version's construct is measured. There is no LLM, no targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance, and no recovery attack by fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization or prompting. For random forget sets the oracle should keep test-level forget accuracy, so 'near chance' is not even the target. Its results are a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that gradient-ascent (DA) unlearning often fails because forget and retain sets are statistically dependent. For random sets, degrading forget metrics necessarily harms test performance. In correlated settings, DA can diverge from the oracle, even ending further away than the original model, or trap the model in inferior minima. They suggest rewinding or noise-based methods as alternatives.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates GA and GDA unlearning baselines, but on ResNet-9/CIFAR-10 using KLoM rather than LLM targeted-knowledge accuracy and recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Forget-set composition and size; learning rate and fine-tuning duration/early stopping. The authors emphasize that high-influence sets are harder to unlearn and that selecting runs after observing the target metric can create a false appearance of success.

fits_no_version.finding: On ResNet-9/CIFAR-10, GA and GDA sample unlearning mostly either stays near the pretrained model or breaks it (validation KLoM rises). High-influence 1st-PC sets show no runs with unlearning signs. Random small sets look unlearned only under post-hoc hyperparameter and stopping selection. SCRUB stays near pretrained. Logistic-regression theory shows DA solutions move away from the retrain oracle when forget and retain data are correlated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ascent-based sample unlearning fails to approximate the retrain oracle without degrading the model, because forget and retain data are statistically dependent. Failure is worst for high-influence or correlated forget sets.

record.problems: The experiments are on image classifiers, not LLM targeted knowledge. Results are primarily plots without per-configuration tabulated values. KLoM measures distributional similarity to oracle models rather than chance-level targeted accuracy, and no recovery attacks are tested.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 1–3 and 7 are not separately expanded into duplicate per-configuration rows where their settings overlap Figure 6. Figure 7 reports retain-set KLoM and says its patterns are nearly identical to Figure 6; figure values are not tabulated.

untested.parts: No LLM, no targeted-knowledge accuracy vs chance, no general-capability benchmark, no recovery attacks. Only oracle-similarity (KLoM) for image-classifier sample unlearning.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocking vs deletion.
No prompting, rephrasing, jailbreak or in-context recovery.
No counter-method evaluated against recovery attacks. The authors only suggest rewinding or noise-based methods as alternatives.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's versions (V1) don't exist; all rows are relinked to none. Section 3 mentions ResNet-18 and ImageNet-Living-17 results, but none appear in the supplied text. The MNIST/FashionMNIST table correctly compares pretrained vs oracle and is not an unlearning result. Peer-reviewed at NeurIPS 2025.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure targeted accuracy against chance or test recovery by attacks; evaluates similarity to the oracle and validation/retain-set performance instead.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
No robust counter-method evaluation against the specified attacks.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Small random forget sets; Gradient Ascent runs
reader_labels.reason: Some runs improve forget-set KLoM, but the authors report significant model degradation and sensitivity to learning rate and stopping; see R01 and R04.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The authors report no realizations showing unlearning signs on the highly important points and describe GA/GDA as either not moving substantially or severely degrading performance; see R13 and R14.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: SCRUB across the plotted CIFAR-10 forget sets
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that SCRUB runs remain close to the pretrained model in KLoM, rather than approaching the oracle; see R03, R06, R09, R12, R15, R18, R21, R24 and R27.
